Independent bounded dual replay: for each of the 6^4 labeled trees (Prüfer sequences), choose each of the 2^5 edge signs at Euclidean edge length, solve the resulting differences with f(v0)=0, discard potentials violating any of the 15 pair constraints, and maximize pairwise output quotients over the remaining potentials. The tight-edge graph at a polytope vertex must be connected, so it contains a spanning tree. There were 354 feasible signed-tree patterns including duplicates. Candidate maxima on mixed and midpoint pairs were respectively 1.029346317584997 and 0.981685480829087; for endpoint averaging, 1.035084657640491 and 1 to rounding.
correctness.rationale: The reflection fixing a midpoint pairs the six vertices into three orbits. After averaging, the signed coefficients sum to one. For the three orbit representatives, test distance-to-the-vertex functions. The sums across the three tests of the distances at each reflection-pair column are all 4+2 sqrt(3). These signed linear inequalities sum to the claimed lower bound even without positivity (and already work for a single midpoint). Solving the three equioscillation equations gives the stated a,b,c; the middle row fixes B and the end-row difference fixes A-C, while their sum fixes L. Simple rational square-root enclosures give a>b>c>0. The given convolution is a probability law and gives coefficients (a,a,b,c,c,b) exactly. Translation-invariant transport contracts under this convolution, and shifts by 1,2,3 of the original two-vertex measures admit couplings with costs sqrt(3)/2, 3/2, sqrt(3), exactly the midpoint distances. Mixed pairs attain L by transporting to a single vertex; vertex pairs have ratio one. For endpoint averaging the far vertex ratio (2+sqrt(3))/sqrt(13) dominates all other pairs and is strictly larger than L.
residual_risks: The independent dual enumeration used floating-point feasibility (tolerance 1e-10); exact equalities and the signed lower bound rely on the analytic argument. The frozen interval checker corroborates near-agreement numerically in its pair identities; it is not the exact proof of them.

value.rationale: The regular hexagon and all its edge midpoints are a canonical Euclidean refinement. The contribution is not just the small gain over averaging: the local bound for arbitrary signed operators is obtained by a positive simultaneous operator without a midpoint-pair obstruction. This identifies the exact simultaneous norm and shows why using only the two nearby vertices is insufficient for the sharp constant.
residual_risks: This does not yield a formula for arbitrary polygon order or all minimizers.
